query: Unit tests for an Arduino Uno module: 10-LED bouncing chaser. Pins: pin 2 OUTPUT LED 0; pin 3 OUTPUT LED 1; pin 4 OUTPUT LED 2; pin 5 OUTPUT LED 3; pin 6 OUTPUT LED 4; pin 7 OUTPUT LED 5; pin 8 OUTPUT LED 6; pin 9 OUTPUT LED 7; pin 10 OUTPUT LED 8; pin 11 OUTPUT LED 9. Arduino API used: digitalRead, digitalWrite, pinMode. Libraries: none. Functions to test: void chaser_init(), void chaser_all_off(), bool chaser_light_only(uint8_t index), void chaser_step(), int8_t chaser_position(), int8_t chaser_direction(), uint8_t chaser_count_on().

Testing digital pins on the Arduino Uno / Covering a function

## Covering a function
- Call the module's init function at the start of every test so that tests do not depend on each other.
- For every output a function drives, assert each pin it should set and each pin it should leave unchanged.
- For functions with an index or a range argument (LED number, state number), test the first value, the last
  value and one value outside the range.

chunks.text:
Testing digital pins on the Arduino Uno / Pin numbers on the Uno

## Pin numbers on the Uno
- Digital pins 0 to 13. The analog inputs A0 to A5 are also digital pins 14 to 19.
- Pins 0 and 1 are the Serial RX/TX lines; the test protocol uses Serial, so tests must not drive them.
- PWM pins: 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11. `LED_BUILTIN` is pin 13.
- Check outputs against the pin numbers in the module's specification (its pin table), not against constants
  taken from the code under test: a wrong pin number in the code is only detected if the test uses the pin
  number the hardware is actually wired to.

For Loop Iteration (aka The Knight Rider)

# For Loop Iteration (aka The Knight Rider)

Often you want to iterate over a series of pins and do something to each one.  For instance, this example blinks 6 LEDs  attached to the Arduino by using a  [**for()**](https://www.arduino.cc/reference/en/language/structure/control-structure/for/) loop to cycle back and forth through digital pins 2-7. The LEDS are turned on and off, in sequence, by using both the [digitalWrite()](https://www.arduino.cc/en/Reference/DigitalWrite)  and [delay()](https://www.arduino.cc/reference/en/language/functions/time/delay/) functions .

We also call this example "[Knight Rider](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KITT)" in memory of a TV-series from the 80's where David Hasselhoff had an AI machine named KITT driving his Pontiac. The car had been augmented with plenty of LEDs in all possible sizes performing flashy effects. In particular, it had a display that scanned back and forth across a line, as shown in this exciting [fight between KITT and KARR](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PO5E5mQIy_Q). This example duplicates the KITT display.
